purpose: Replace generic shared Fellowship equipment silhouettes with dedicated project-owned character equipment while retaining existing modular fallback, future skeletal-rig handoff and low-spec performance contracts.
continuity_rule: Equipment dressing reinforces established film character identity; it does not create new plot actions, powers, loot tiers or alternate outcomes.

Sam.identity: practical hobbit equipment and load-bearing travel silhouette

Merry.identity: distinct companion cloak and compact hobbit blade

Pippin.identity: lighter youthful cloak/blade silhouette distinct from Merry

Aragorn.identity: weathered ranger layers and mixed scout/melee equipment

Boromir.identity: soldier silhouette with strong shield/sword read without villain coding

Legolas.identity: slender ranged silhouette, bow and close weapon with economical movement

Gimli.identity: compact heavy dwarf mass, beard volume and axe/helmet read

behavior: Existing common project-owned assets remain fallback if a dedicated package is absent.
M_ProductionSurface runtime instances retain separate cloth/wood/leather/metal response.
Existing cloak/prop procedural motion continues to animate dedicated meshes.
Valid skeletal mesh + AnimBP still override the entire modular fallback path.

performance: No new skeletal simulation or dynamic cloth solver is enabled.
Equipment remains on existing bounded static-mesh components.
No new per-frame asset loads beyond the existing one-time style application path.
Future final rigs use sockets/LOD/URO and replace, not duplicate, fallback equipment.
